annotations.text:
PICKED (2026-09-01): B — tabs on the card, contingent on the authoring being cheap.
Still clickable. A and C live on the Alternates page; the authoring options are on the Authoring page.

TOP ROW — how a card GETS its tabs (pick one or both):
G1 Select & combine: tick rows in Prep, one action groups them. Works anywhere, discoverable, no drag skill. Tradeoff: checkboxes are new chrome on the Page view.
G2 Drag onto the card: board-native, matches the World tree's drag-into gesture, previews the tabs in place. Tradeoff: only exists on the board; drop-on vs drop-between needs care.

BOTTOM ROW — easing add -> organize (independent of G1/G2):
O1 rail: organize without leaving Prep; costs page width.
O2 born placed: kills the organizing step for most adds; add-row gets busier.
O3 one surface: the merge question, tradeoffs on the sketch. Reviewer evidence says keep the board (weeknight-DM 'keep this'); nobody asked for a merge.

A — STATE STRIP (not picked)
One scene-level strip; chips = variants; empty = show everything.
Kept for reference: it is still the honest picture of the scene-level data model, and could return as a read-only summary line even under B.

C — EVERYTHING VISIBLE (not picked)
No state ever hides; live state carries the ink.
Kept for reference: closest to how Kilmarn was actually run.
